We called to request a quote, and we arranged to meet Iñaki at 11:00. Ten minutes before, he called back saying he was in a hurry and would arrive around 1:30 PM. We never heard from him again. The next day, I called the office. After several attempts, they finally answered. The woman told me her colleagues weren't there and that they would contact me. The following day, Iñaki called again, apologizing and saying that if I had time to come to Vitoria the next day, he would call me. We're still waiting for that call. He also mentioned that since it was a leak, Novanor might not cover it, but he would give me advice and put me in touch with a professional.

I don't think this lack of professionalism is normal for a company that specializes in dampness. It seems they don't consider it worthwhile for small issues...

A shame and a disappointment.

one_star_reviews.text:
Everything was awful. We drove into the parking garage with the car battery at 3%, desperately searching for a charging point. We found one inside, but it didn't work at all. Some staff members came to help us, but they had no idea how it worked and it was of little use. Then they took us to another spot, and the same thing happened: none of the chargers worked inside these parking garages, and none of the employees knew how to use them. What a disgrace! We paid €2.50 for nothing, just to get in. In the end, the only solution they offered was to take us to a hotel with private chargers, where we had to spend a fortune. The service is terrible. We will never again enter this negligent parking garage where absolutely nothing works; the barrier wouldn't even open with the ticket they gave us. Why pay the parking fee and then have to spend an additional €30 to charge at a hotel? A truly awful experience.

one_star_reviews.text: I can't give them a lower rating because I can't. They have an employee with absolutely no empathy; her name is Natalia. She laughs at the difficulties someone might have in fulfilling a contract and treats you like a bad payer. Obviously, when you take out a loan, it's because you can afford it, but life also throws up unexpected events that complicate things, and when that happens, you need time, which they don't give you. It's no wonder they have the reviews they do if they treat everyone the same... You have to know how to distinguish between people who are shameless and people who care about paying their debts. At the very least, respond politely and try to make things easy for them to pay. It's very sad to forget that the person you're talking to is a person just like you and that tomorrow those same problems could happen to you too.

one_star_reviews.text:
After many years, and since my grandparents have been here, I'm dissatisfied with the care and management of this residence. Every so often, we find that some service or professional is missing, and no one is put in place to replace them.

I want to make a special mention of the physiotherapy service. We went many months without a physiotherapist. They finally hired someone, but after barely two months, we were without this service again, and it's been a very long time since then, with no apparent effort to resolve the situation. I believe this is a very important service for the residents and shouldn't be neglected for so long.

We've also been without a social worker for months, and now there's no hairdressing service either, with no apparent search for replacements or solutions.

The saddest thing has been having to manage certain procedures after losing my grandfather and being forced to call from one place to another to get help with the paperwork. Even after calling another center for guidance, the response was that those procedures had to be handled by our residence, even though we don't have a social worker. In such difficult times, expecting a little support and guidance shouldn't be too much to ask.

I want to especially acknowledge Daniel, who does everything he can and goes out of his way to help with everything we ask of him. But it's also true that he can't take on responsibilities outside his job description and needs the necessary support.

On the other hand, we are incredibly lucky with the staff at the center. They are lovely, do their jobs very well, and treat the residents with great care, respect, and compassion. That's precisely why it's so sad that the lack of staff and certain services ends up affecting the residents and their families.

I sincerely hope that measures are taken and the management of these services is improved, because both the residents and their families deserve comprehensive and stable care, and above all, to feel supported when they need it.

I am a resident who is hemiplegic and I need a physiotherapist. The one we had left more than two months ago and we still haven't had one. The staff is wonderful, and the director is too. It's a lack of will on the part of those responsible for hiring.

one_star_reviews.text: I'm calling because I'm feeling unwell and they never answer the phone.
It's normal that NO ONE answers the phone at this center; you call for an urgent need and there's no way to get through. The public sector is rotten.

They only answer the phone from 8:30 to 9:15, more or less. After that time, it's impossible to contact the mental health center. The call rings two or three times and then, suspiciously, it drops, like when you reject a call on your cell phone. Other times, it rings six or eight times and then drops. If you need to go to the emergency room, ask for information about medication, or make an appointment, it's best to go directly, as they are never available by phone, except during the aforementioned time slot. The strangest thing is that they have two sheets of paper on the wall saying that if we can't go, we should call so that someone else can take the appointment. But of course, if it's so difficult to call and get through, how are you supposed to cancel the appointment? It's impossible, really. There's a woman at reception who is rather rude to us. I already filed a complaint with the SIP (Institute of Psychological Services) yesterday, and if things continue the same way, I will file a complaint with the Ombudsman. Greuges, let's see if they listen at that mental health center. We all have to do that, file complaints.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with Nerea Rapado during my divorce proceedings was very negative, and based solely on what happened in my case, I would not recommend her services.

One of the aspects that harmed me the most was the wording of the agreement.

The divorce agreement stipulated that I would retain 100% ownership of the house and that I would have to pay the other party the amount corresponding to their share of the property. The agreement stated that this money was due upon my leaving the house.

However, even though the lawyer herself knew that I didn't have that money, as she asked me about it about five times, and that I needed bank financing to be able to make the payment, no deadline or condition was included that would make the payment contingent on the bank having previously approved and disbursed the financing. Furthermore, much of the content of the agreement had already been agreed upon in April, but the negotiation dragged on until the end of June. The lawyer was aware of my need for financing, the procedural timeline, and that court ratification was not expected until the end of September. Despite this, the agreement stipulated that payment would be due the moment the other party vacated the property, without allowing any additional time for the bank to complete the transaction. In my opinion, this lack of foresight left me vulnerable to default because I wouldn't have the funds available when the payment was due.

This situation caused me enormous concern because the payment obligation arose upon leaving the property, regardless of whether I had the money from the bank or not.

The problems continued afterward.

The divorce agreement itself established that I would be awarded 100% ownership of the property. Despite this, I was later told that a deed of sale for the property had to be executed before a notary and that the other party had to be present to sign it before the bank could release the funds to me.

When I refused to sign the deed before a notary, I was told that the transaction couldn't proceed and that legal action would have to be initiated to force the other party to sign.

Following this advice, legal proceedings were initiated, which resulted in additional legal and procedural costs, as well as added time and worry.

Given my situation, I decided to consult another lawyer.

This second lawyer, after reviewing the documentation, explained that in my case, the divorce agreement already legally established the transfer of 100% ownership of the property to me and that it wasn't necessary to complete the sale before a notary as I had been advised.

Following this new lawyer's advice, I was finally able to resolve a situation that had been stalled for some time.

I can't say for sure what the reasons were for certain decisions made during my case, but I can certainly comment on the service I received: I completely lost faith in this lawyer's advice.

When someone hires a lawyer, they expect them to anticipate potential problems, adequately protect their interests, and provide sound advice before signing agreements with significant financial consequences.

In my case, I believe that didn't happen.

Terrible experience with this property management company. They charge €84.70 for a certificate of payment for my parking space, a totally abusive and out of market price for a standardized document.
I sent them an email expressing my disagreement with the amount and they didn't even give me any explanation, they just said that if I wanted the document I had to pay.
To top it off, it took them 7 days to get it and when I went to their office in person on the seventh day, they didn't even have it. They had to generate it instantly, showing that it is a procedure that is done in two minutes from their database and at no cost.
In any other administration this document is free or has a symbolic cost of around €20/30. It's a shame how they take advantage of owners who make payments on time, coupled with zero customer service and no efficiency. Not recommended at all.

⭐ A terrible experience. Honestly, it's hard to understand how a real estate agency can operate with this level of unprofessionalism.

The delays are constant and, at times, excessive. They don't respect agreed-upon schedules, they don't honor their commitments, and getting them to answer the phone can be a real ordeal.

The worst part isn't an occasional delay, which can happen to anyone, but rather that this lack of punctuality, communication, and professionalism is repeated time and time again.

When you're dealing with something as important as a home, you expect professionalism, trustworthiness, and a minimum of respect for the client's time. My experience has been the exact opposite.

Personally, after what I've been through, I would never work with this agency again, and I certainly cannot recommend them.

one_star_reviews.text:
We were familiar with the Redemptorists and their work in a couple of Latin American countries, and during our visit to Santa Gadea del Cid, the QR codes distributed throughout the town included information about the Monastery of Our Lady of the Thorn, run by this missionary congregation dedicated to prayer, evangelization, formation, and preaching of the Catholic faith.

The QR codes in Santa Gadea tell us that Our Lady of the Thorn appeared to a shepherd, stating that she wanted a place of worship built on that spot. However, the shepherd, fearing disbelief, said nothing.
The Virgin appeared to him again, this time with a group of friars, who reprimanded the shepherd. He then recounted what he had seen, and construction of the Monastery of Our Lady of the Thorn began in 1399. After passing through the hands of several congregations, experiencing abandonment, confiscation of church property, and even occupation by troops, it is currently managed by the Redemptorist missionaries. But to our unpleasant surprise, upon arrival, we found the church reserved for private use and inaccessible to visitors.
The cloister and monastic buildings are shared by the clergy and those who book weddings and events, but are off-limits to the public.
We could only see the exterior grounds, within the complex but separate from the main building. Even so, we were politely asked to leave even those exterior areas because the venue was exclusively booked for a wedding.

In the end, we managed to take some photos of the exterior and then of the walls from the outside. I have no problem with it being a private business, but it was completely unrelated and a disappointment for anyone hoping to learn about history, visit an artistic building, complete a tourist visit to Santa Gadea del Cid, or even simply enjoy a Catholic monastery.

In any case, what we were able to see of the entire complex is geared towards economic exploitation, with nothing to do with evangelization, Catholicism, or the enjoyment of artistic heritage. Their website includes a mobile phone number for contact, and, like any venue that hosts private celebrations, they allow preliminary visits to finalize the booking. Hopefully, visits can also be scheduled through this channel at times that don't interfere with business.

Reservation recommended
No

one_star_reviews.text:
I was previously a student at this school and have now finished my time as a student. I consider that the Primary Education stage was very good and that, in general, I had a positive experience during those years. However, my opinion about Secondary Education is completely different, since, according to my experience, it has been a very negative stage.

Regarding learning, I do not consider it satisfactory, since, in my opinion, many of the things that can really be useful for the future are not taught.

Furthermore, one of the most negative aspects of the school is the dining service. I consider that the food is not in good conditions and that, on some occasions, food from days or even weeks ago is served. The menu hardly changes and the students are forced to eat food that, personally, I consider to be of very poor quality.

On the other hand, the dining room monitors are excessively strict. For example, if a student spills water on their food, they are forced to eat it anyway.

Honestly, I think Primary Education is great, but I wouldn't recommend Secondary Education. As a former student, I feel like I learned practically nothing during this stage, despite always being an excellent student and achieving good academic results.

one_star_reviews.text:
Terrible is an understatement. I went there for a termination of pregnancy, and it felt more like I was going for a vehicle inspection than a clinic that treats people in vulnerable situations. Aside from the curt and almost inhuman treatment—not to mention the complete lack of it—it seems like the entire clinic staff is bitter about their jobs and life. I didn't even see the doctor who performed the procedure; I DIDN'T SEE OR GET TO KNOW THE DOCTOR! When they administered the sedation, I burst into tears from the pain caused by the anesthesiologist inserting the cannula. She didn't reassure me or speak to me at any point. I fell asleep sobbing uncontrollably, and when I woke up, the nurses abruptly and roughly took me to some suspicious beds because I doubt they even change the sheets.
In the room with the beds, there was a television playing a series that made absolutely no sense in an environment and situation like this. After a while, they gave me a pack of wipes to clean the blood from my vagina, which I had to throw on the floor because there was nowhere to put them.
YOU DON'T NEED TO RESPOND WITH THE TYPICAL MESSAGE OF "WE'RE SORRY FOR THE TREATMENT YOU RECEIVED AND WE'LL PASS ON THE MESSAGE," because you won't. This clinic is a dump, with staff who lack the necessary tools to deal with people in vulnerable situations. At my next appointment at my local health center, I plan to tell them to remove this clinic from the list so it can provide a proper public service. SHAMEFUL.

Today I went to get a vaginal Doppler ultrasound, and when I arrived the doctor told me they don't do them. How is it possible that the reception staff or the people in charge of providing information to the public don't know what tests are done at the clinic? They've made me waste my whole morning, because it's not just the travel but everything involved in attending a medical appointment.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with this property management company as a tenant has been very negative, especially regarding the handling of certain issues during my tenancy and the way the contract termination and security deposit return were managed.

During my time in the apartment, I had a significant damp problem in the bathroom, which I reported to the management company and followed up on. The problem wasn't resolved for an extended period, and I had to live with the dampness for quite some time.

Finally, after a lawyer intervened, a repair was carried out. The people responsible for the repair told me that the problem stemmed from a faulty installation of the shower screen, which was allowing water to leak in. The situation even began to affect our health.

I find it particularly concerning that an issue of this nature, related to the condition of the apartment, had to reach the point of requiring legal intervention to finally get it addressed. In my opinion, a property management company should show greater diligence and follow-up when faced with problems that directly affect the living conditions and well-being of its tenants.

The situation became complicated again at the end of the contract. I handed over the apartment completely empty and in very good condition, which was verified during the key handover.

I had paid €1,800 between the security deposit and additional guarantee. Initially, I received €900, while the remaining €900 was pending. Over the following weeks, I had to follow up several times to get clear information about the status of this amount.

Regarding the outstanding utilities, I provided the invoices and proposed that the corresponding amount be settled using the €900 that was still being held. Finally, after insisting in writing and copying the owner of the property management company, the matter was resolved, and I received the corresponding balance once the utilities were settled.

I want to emphasize that the financial issue was finally resolved. My complaint isn't that the property manager kept my money, but rather the lack of communication, the delays, and the unnecessary difficulty in resolving situations that, in my opinion, should have been handled much more clearly and professionally.

As a tenant, I believe that a property manager should properly monitor issues affecting the property and show particular diligence when these could affect the well-being of the residents. In my experience, I had to insist repeatedly and ultimately seek legal advice to get a major issue addressed.

Based on my personal experience, I would not recommend this property manager to other tenants.

We rented the apartment for five and a half years, and our experience with the management was disappointing from the start.

Upon moving in, we reported several issues: a leak from the shower screen into the master bedroom, a bathroom door that wouldn't close, damaged kitchen baseboards, problems with the bedroom wall, and a broken balcony awning mechanism. We had to send several emails to get attention, and some issues weren't resolved until they worsened, such as when the laminate flooring started to peel due to sun exposure.

After two years (2022), we were notified of a cumulative rent increase of 6.3% (based on the Consumer Price Index), even though there was a 2% limit at the time. When we checked the Official State Gazette (BOE), the explanation we received was that they had "given us some consideration due to the pandemic," something we found difficult to understand considering we moved into the apartment well after the state of emergency was declared.

The most worrying situation occurred during my nearly seven-month pregnancy, when dampness reappeared from the bathroom, affecting the master bedroom where we slept. We reported it, but received no response, ultimately requiring our lawyer to intervene to find a solution.

When our son was one year old, a leak from the neighbor's bathroom damaged the wall of his room. The insurance company repaired the damage and, unable to find matching baseboards, compensated us with almost €300 to replace them all. We reported this to the building management, but they never resolved the issue, and we went two more years without the piece being replaced.

Ultimately, the most frustrating aspect has been the lack of timely responses, the poor follow-up on incidents, and the lack of transparency. After five and a half years, our experience with this management has been highly unsatisfactory, and we expected a much more professional and diligent approach.

I had never experienced anything like this.

After weeks of discussions, we received written confirmation that the apartment was ours. A specific date and time were set for signing the contract, and, trusting this, we made purchases for the property, organized the move, and stopped looking for other options.

During the process, we were even put in contact with the previous tenant to negotiate the purchase of their furniture, all before the contract was signed, which further reinforced our confidence that the deal was finalized.

On the very day scheduled for signing, the transaction was unilaterally canceled, with the owner claiming they wanted to inspect the property and then decide whether or not to rent it.

Since then, we have requested written explanations without receiving a clear answer about what happened.

Everyone can draw their own conclusions. Our experience has resulted in a significant loss of time, financial losses, and personal and professional damage that we have now had to pursue through the appropriate channels.

I hope no one else has to go through a similar situation.

A very bad experience with the service I received this morning at the Gaspar Aguilar branch.

I went there to make a tax payment using the bank's ATM and asked for help from the teller. The service was extremely poor: they practically didn't let me explain what I needed and responded automatically, without stopping to listen or try to find a solution.

What surprised me most was that, since it was a transaction that had to be done at the bank's ATM and using a service offered by the bank, the teller wasn't even able to get up from their desk to show me how to do it correctly. They didn't even bother to ask if I was a customer.

I completely understand that there are internal procedures and limitations on certain transactions, but attending to the customer, listening to their problem, and trying to guide them should be the bare minimum.

I am a customer of the bank, and after the service I received today, I have decided to close my account and not open another one with this bank.

It's a shame that a private entity loses customers because of this kind of service. The employees who deal directly with the public represent the bank and, through their actions, should also represent and protect the interests of the institution they work for. My impression is quite the opposite.

They're not even good enough to fix a bicycle. I had to take my car to this garage because it was the one that honored the warranty. I took it in four times, and each time it came out worse. I took it in because it was leaking transmission fluid. When they tried to "fix" the problem, they created an even worse one. It's an automatic transmission, and they caused the gears to skip. I took the car back, and they replaced the clutch because supposedly that was the problem. The skidding stopped, but it started leaking fluid again. On top of all that, the first time they lost the wheel stud, and now they've lost the sump guard too. The car sat in the garage for a while to see if they'd fix it, but they didn't. They even left it parked without disconnecting the battery, and I had to buy a new one because of their negligence. I'm taking the car back just as broken as when I brought it in, and with fewer parts because they're terrible workers. I absolutely do not recommend them. When they respond to complaints, it's just to say they don't have time, and they take no responsibility for anything.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience at the FIVAP clinic in La Laguna was deeply disappointing and emotionally draining. In a process as delicate as fertility treatment, I expected professionalism, coordination, medical follow-up, and empathy, but the reality was very different.

During the treatment, I was seen by different professionals who, on numerous occasions, were unaware of my medical history, the tests I had undergone, or the decisions I had previously made. I perceived a clear lack of coordination, contradictions among professionals, and a lack of involvement from the doctor in charge, who frequently delegated care.

In addition, the staff generally treated me coldly, distantly, and, at times, unpleasantly. I experienced particularly uncomfortable situations, such as being reprimanded in the waiting room for an appointment that the clinic itself had tried to reschedule the day before, despite having arranged it weeks in advance and having adjusted my vacation to attend. I also suffered inconsiderate appointment changes, repeated confusion regarding my name, and errors in my personal information, even on the day of the egg retrieval.

Overall, I felt there was a lack of individualized attention, organization, and sensitivity towards patients. The only notable exception was Dr. Jean Paul, whose approach I found more personal, respectful, and humane.

Given that it's a private clinic and the process carries such a heavy emotional and financial burden, I believe the care should be much more rigorous and personalized.

Based on my experience, I wouldn't recommend this center. Fertility treatment is difficult enough without adding the uncertainty, disorganization, and emotional strain I experienced.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very basic self-service dog wash. If you go, make sure you bring plenty of coins, as there is no other way to pay, and bring your own towels, as none are provided.

There are only three functions: wash with shampoo, rinse and dry. The biggest thing to be aware of is that although the STOP button stops whichever function you’re using, it does not pause your paid time. The countdown keeps running. So if you stop the water to properly massage the shampoo into your dog’s coat before rinsing, you’re still paying for that time. At €2 for only 3 minutes, it disappears very quickly.

The dryer was also disappointing — the air felt cold on my dog while the handle became surprisingly hot in my hand.

I’ve used other self-service dog washes with conditioner/antiparasitic treatments, better drying equipment, brushes and the ability to actually pause the paid time. Compared with those, this one feels extremely basic for the price.

So: bring coins, bring towels, and remember that STOP stops the machine, not the clock.

one_star_reviews.text:
I've been a regular customer at this salon for a year and a half. I've always understood that their work is tiring and demanding, so I've never minded them not being friendly, and it's something I've always tolerated as long as the service was good. However, what happened to me today was completely unacceptable.

The person who attended to me asked me to relax my hand while cutting my nails. I politely explained that I suffer from anxiety and that my fingers tense up involuntarily. Far from showing even a modicum of empathy or professionalism, she started talking and complaining about me in her language to the colleague next to her, making me feel extremely uncomfortable.

Even though I clarified that it was a completely unconscious act (and knowing perfectly well that she understands Spanish), she stopped cutting my nails, started blowing on them in a huff and puff of indignation, and began filing them roughly and aggressively. I find this to be an absolute lack of respect for a customer. I will not tolerate such treatment, not from her or anyone else.

I am very disappointed that, after so much time, this woman treats me with such disrespect.

From my point of view, this is just another public institution that doesn't like to work.
I've called during office hours approximately 100 times, and they haven't answered the phone, not even to tell me they can't get through.
Seriously, they don't take into account people with mobility issues or those who can't attend the center for three hours a day.

one_star_reviews.text:
They don't have communion rails so people can receive Communion kneeling, nor can the faithful kneel in the pews during the consecration or to pray.
Communion rails are not an aesthetic whim, priests. They are a visible sign of faith, a place where the body expresses what the soul believes: that before Christ in the Eucharist, one adores, loves, and reveres Him.
The Church did not prohibit communion rails. Some people simply find them inconvenient.
Confession doesn't exist here. Another victory for Satan. They hold collective forgiveness ceremonies a couple of times a year and that's it. Could there be a greater folly? Let's remember that the devil doesn't like souls to go to confession. They also don't recite the prayer to Saint Michael the Archangel at the end of Mass for protection against the devil's snares. Satan must be pleased.
They don't have holy water so people can bless themselves upon entering or leaving the church.

As in so many other places, communion is distributed like crackers, handed out while standing, as if the Divinity of Our Lord didn't deserve the utmost respect. The particles of the Lord's Body that remain in people's hands or that might fall to the ground and be trampled are of no concern to them whatsoever. Such irreverence and sacrilege are appalling.
The church resembles a marketplace before and after Mass. There is no recollection or silence.
The priests try to cover all this up by being very friendly, and many people focus on this and nothing else, forgetting the doctrine of our Holy Catholic Church.

We need to pray many Rosaries for this parish. They are spiritually asleep. I went to the 8:00 PM Mass, but since I was alone, "people got distracted and there's no one there." Even if there's ONE PERSON there, Mass should be celebrated. The parish priests take two weeks off and leave us without the Eucharist. At Mass time, they say three lines and it lasts 15 minutes, 20 if you're lucky. It's a disgrace 😳. They haven't even bothered with the holy water. They're stripping Christianity of everything sacred.

Honestly, I felt like I threw €120 away. I planned this session with such enthusiasm to have a beautiful memory of my daughter's first birthday, and it ended up being a huge disappointment.

I booked the session because I needed the edited photos before the birthday, and when the date arrived, they weren't delivered. The worst part was the lack of communication: after I paid, she stopped responding, and I had to chase her down to get an answer.

The session itself wasn't a good experience either. Since it was a session with a baby, I really missed having more patience and sensitivity. In addition, the studio was very hot and quite neglected, and some of the equipment looked old.

I also paid an extra €20 for a cake for the session that was rock hard, which only made an already unpleasant experience worse.

It was my daughter's first birthday, a memory that was very special to me and my family, and I ended up completely disappointed because I couldn't send the photos on her birthday. I hired her because she promised to have them ready before the date. I was very dissatisfied with both the service and the customer service.

I wouldn't hire her again, and I certainly wouldn't recommend her to any family.

one_star_reviews.text: They were incredibly incompetent. I took them a vintage monitor I own as a collector's item to have the image adjusted, and aside from having to chase after them to see if it was finished, they lost the original power cable and didn't even bother to look for it. They even told me they don't usually take cables when you bring in equipment. When I left the monitor, I asked, "Should I leave the cable too?" Their indifferent response was, "Well... yes... whatever you want..." (You should have told me when you didn't need the cable... that would have been the logical thing to do). On top of that, they returned the monitor with the audio connection board loose, without screws. I noticed it right there, pointed it out, and they just slapped on whatever screws they could find. It's not a big deal, but it's another problem. And to top it all off, I got home with the monitor, tested it, and to my surprise, the image was still misaligned. I went back to the store to complain, and they told me it might have gotten misaligned during the trip, that it happens sometimes (the trip was from the store to my car, which was right next to the store, a 20-minute drive, and from the garage to my apartment, which I just had to take the elevator to. I find it very strange that the image would be misaligned without me having touched the monitor, but that was their explanation). After all the hassle and unprofessionalism, I asked for a refund, and they told me the repair was under warranty and that I should bring it back, which I obviously wasn't going to do. After all that, spending more gas and leaving a monitor like that in a place I don't trust... no thanks, I'd rather lose my money. Not recommended at all.

one_star_reviews.text:
Unfortunately, we had a very disappointing experience at Terra at The St. Regis Mardavall Mallorca Resort.

The hotel itself is beautiful, and we were there for the spa. It was raining extremely heavily that day, so rather than walking to another restaurant nearby, we decided to have lunch at Terra.

The prices were extremely high for what we received. I ordered a bacon cheeseburger with fries and a small portion of coleslaw, and it cost around €40. For that price, especially at a five-star hotel, I expected the food and service to be excellent.

Unfortunately, the food also took a long time to arrive, and when it finally reached our table, both the burger and fries were cold. The portions were quite small as well.

I also asked our waiter what the seeds in the coleslaw were. Nobody on the staff seemed to know, and although they said they would find out, they never came back with an answer.

To make things worse, it took a very long time just to receive my change after paying, and when it finally came back, the amount was incorrect and €1 short.

For the prices being charged, the food and level of service were nowhere near what I would expect from a restaurant inside a five-star hotel. The resort itself was lovely, but based on our experience, I unfortunately would not recommend Terra for lunch.
Up to 10 min

I didn't want to leave a review because I don't like to harm anyone's work, but seeing the lack of involvement with our community, I think the least I can do is share my experience as it is.

Our experience has been quite bad. There are messages that have gone unanswered for months, even after repeated follow-ups, speaking with her in person, and her apologies.

For about four years, there haven't been any residents' meetings or changes in president because meetings simply haven't been called. We had to force them to hold a meeting to change the president and also to approve many expenses that they approved without consulting the residents first.

Furthermore, when you need to talk to her or resolve something, she's almost never available, if ever. She only reacts when you're forced to file a complaint or formal grievance. She has set hours, but I've gone several times during those hours and she wasn't there.

Overall, very poor organization, poor communication, zero follow-up, and ZERO involvement. For a service the community is paying for, it leaves much to be desired.

To this day, I'm still waiting for a response to several messages I've sent (I hope they'll reply after reading this review). I find it unprofessional and disrespectful to the residents.

Personally, I would strongly recommend changing management companies. I'm giving them 1 star out of courtesy, because the app won't let me give them 0.

one_star_reviews.text:
I was considering taking out a mortgage with them. I consider myself to have a good profile, with a solvent financial situation, and I had other options on the table.

That is precisely why I contacted Caixa Guissona. The fact that it is a smaller, local and cooperative entity made me think that I would find a more personal and close treatment and, above all, more flexibility than in a large bank. Honestly, I expected this to be one of its strong points.

But the reality has been quite different. I have found a less personal treatment and very little negotiation capacity.

The proposal they made me was more expensive than other options that I am studying and, when I asked if the conditions could be reviewed or improved taking into account my profile, the answer was that the conditions are closed and non-negotiable.

Here I was quite surprised. I understand perfectly well that an entity has certain rates and criteria, but if a small entity also has no room to negotiate a transaction with a good profile, I don't see what the differential value is compared to going directly to a large entity.

In addition, they confirmed to me that in order to formalize the mortgage, life insurance was mandatory. In my case, it is a condition that I am not willing to assume. They clarified that I could contract it with another company, but it remains a requirement that makes the transaction unfeasible for me.

In the end, I have decided to continue evaluating other financing alternatives.

I cannot evaluate what the service is like once you are a client because in the end I have not contracted with them. But I can evaluate the process that I have experienced so far and, honestly, I expected much more from the personal treatment, proximity and flexibility of a local and cooperative entity.

Personally, if someone is looking for a mortgage, I would first compare with the best-known entities and with a mortgage comparator or intermediary before assuming that a small, local entity will offer better conditions or more flexibility.

A shame, because I contacted Caixa Guissona hoping to find something different from what the big banks offer and that has not been the case.

one_star_reviews.text:
It's shameful that a patient with borderline personality disorder, who begs her psychiatrist for help because she's having suicidal thoughts again, is being ignored. She's having horrific crises. No one is helping her. What kind of professionals are you?

I'm putting this in writing today, October 11, 2026. My daughter is desperately crying out for help, and no one is helping her. She's asking for medication for depression, and Dr. Maria is refusing. I want to make it clear that if anything happens to my 32-year-old daughter, it's the fault of the center and the unsympathetic doctors. If patients aren't bleeding profusely, covered in blood with numerous cuts, or trying to overdos on pills, no one does anything. It's a sham of help. They're only helping people commit suicide. What kind of worthless doctors are you? If anything happens to my daughter, it's your fault. And I have proof of the thousands of times she's sought help. You know her serious situation and you ignore her. I live in Madrid, but I'm keeping a close eye on her. This will be on TV. Bad people. To be a doctor, you have to have a calling.

It's rubbish, all public services are rubbish. They don't care about the patient. They just go there to put in the hours so they get paid. The receptionists are rude and treat you well or badly depending on your nationality. And the phone is silent all day, every day. I checked once while I was there; I called and it showed up on the reception phone, but silent. They're simply not paid enough to answer calls :) I pray to God that the workers at this center and their families never have to go through what I did... begging for months for an appointment just because I need medication. Being treated like dirt and ignored while suffering from a mental health condition... free healthcare is just a smokescreen.
Awful. My daughter told me the psychologist didn't talk at all, they didn't schedule her appointments, and they didn't include the medication on the prescription. Awful.

A TERRIBLE EXPERIENCE at the MAZDA FORNELLS DE LA SELVA WORKSHOP (Girona).

I took my car in for a routine check-up and ended up going through a real ordeal that lasted from November 21st to January 15th.

No sooner had I left the workshop than a practically new tire (23,000 km) blew out, and they refused to take responsibility. The tire in question had a cut of approximately 6 cm, damage that is not consistent with normal wear and tear and which, given the circumstances, seemed to have been caused accidentally by some kind of tool while the vehicle was in the workshop. To make matters worse, they left me stranded on the street five minutes after closing time, without offering any solution or the slightest bit of help.

Days later, they replaced the tire—at my expense, of course—and during that process, they damaged a rim that was completely new. Instead of properly fixing the problem, they repaired a rim that wasn't damaged at all, later acknowledging their mistake. Even so, the car remained in the workshop for almost another month.

When I finally went to pick up the vehicle, I discovered that the rim still hadn't been repaired, after weeks of waiting, excuses, and constant breaches of promised deadlines.

Xavi, the workshop manager, deserves special mention. The service I received from him was, in my experience, particularly disappointing. I found his attitude rude, arrogant, and unprofessional, with explanations that were contradictory on several occasions and commitments that were later broken. Instead of inspiring confidence and seeking a solution to the problem, his handling of the situation only increased my frustration. I expected a much more serious, transparent, and respectful attitude from the workshop manager.

The lack of professionalism, organization, and transparency was evident throughout the entire process. During this debacle, I had to visit the workshop six times, and on three of those occasions, other customers were complaining, which, at least in my experience, speaks volumes about how things are being managed at that establishment.

Furthermore, the workshop manager only showed up once, despite our repeated requests to speak with him.

Contradictory explanations, a constant stream of delays without any credible explanation, broken promises, and appalling management.

I absolutely do not recommend this workshop. A waste of time, disorganization, poor management, and utterly unacceptable customer service that, in my opinion, tarnishes the reputation of a brand as reputable as Mazda.

If there's one area where human interaction should be fundamental, it's precisely this one. I left and I won't be returning.

one_star_reviews.text:
The ambience at Jacqueline is absolutely incredible. It’s a beautiful space and definitely creates the expectation that you’re about to have a really special experience. Unfortunately, for us, that’s where it ended.

I’m not sure if they were short staffed or if something else was going on, but the service was honestly atrocious. For a restaurant of this caliber, we expected significantly better.

The “dry aged” filet mignon was extremely disappointing. Whatever the aging process may have been, it certainly didn’t eat like a quality dry aged filet. It was easily the toughest filet I’ve ever had and was incredibly difficult to even cut through. The potatoes weren’t fully cooked, and overall the food was mediocre at best.

The one bright spot was the drinks, which were really good.

It’s unfortunate because the atmosphere is incredible and the restaurant has so much potential, but when you’re paying for an elevated dining experience, the food and service need to match the setting. For us, they simply didn’t.

one_star_reviews.text:
A very unpleasant experience. I arrived half an hour before my initial assessment appointment for a delicate and urgent family member's case, and during the 40 minutes I waited, I didn't see anyone at the center who could tell me where or how I should wait. Hearing people inside an office, I knocked on the door 10 minutes after the agreed-upon time.

The woman I assume was Sonia opened the door and, without greeting me, introducing herself, or showing the slightest courtesy, rudely told me to "wait a little while" and slammed the door in my face.

I completely understand that an appointment can be delayed; that wasn't the issue. What I find unacceptable is receiving that kind of treatment from a psychology professional, especially for an initial consultation regarding a sensitive situation. If there's one area where human interaction should be fundamental, it's precisely this one. I left and I won't be returning.

one_star_reviews.text: My kitten passed away on Friday, September 25th, and we wanted to have him cremated so we could keep his ashes at home. I was notified today, September 29th, that I could pick him up from the veterinary hospital where I had taken him. To my dismay, when I arrived home, I opened the cardboard box containing my kitten's remains and found a wooden box with a plastic bag inside filled with his ashes. I don't believe an animal, a member of the family, deserves this treatment, especially considering the price they charge. At the very least, they should have provided a ceramic urn with the ashes in a cloth bag. Or even given us the option to choose the container—something more respectful. I absolutely do not recommend this service. And I hope I never have to deal with this company again.

one_star_reviews.text:
Today, August 21st, at around 9:30 a.m., I called this center to request an appointment for my husband for an evaluation and the creation of orthotic insoles.

During the conversation, I was informed that the first available appointment was for September 28th and that, subsequently, the insoles could take approximately one and a half to two months to arrive. When I simply expressed my surprise at the timeframe—since that would practically mean waiting until December—the response I received was that “this is what we have to do this time of year.”
They then began to explain the prices for the evaluation and the consultation. When I politely pointed out that I hadn't actually asked about the price, I was told that it was their obligation to inform me.
Beyond the waiting times, which I can perfectly understand during the holiday season, what prompted me to write this review is the way I was treated over the phone. At no point did I question their fees or demand an immediate appointment; I was simply requesting information as a potential future client.

I believe that when someone calls inquiring about a center's services, the way they are treated and the manner in which they are handled is fundamental. After this initial contact, I have unfortunately decided not to schedule an appointment or visit this establishment.

I hope this review reaches the center's management, as I believe it would be beneficial to review the telephone service offered to potential clients. Good service begins from the very first contact, even before walking through the door.

one_star_reviews.text:
We were on a road trip through Spain when our van broke down and had to be towed. Our insurance company arranged Grúas Chiva for us, and unfortunately the whole experience was an absolute nightmare.

The initial towing itself was fine. However, we had been told through our insurance that we would be taken together with the vehicle to the nearest city (Castellón), from where we could continue to our campsite in Alcalà de Xivert by public transport. This may have been a misunderstanding or something lost in translation, but when the tow truck arrived we were suddenly told that they could not take us with them.

This left us stranded by the side of the road in the middle of nowhere at around 9 pm, where we had to organise a taxi ourselves. It took us around two hours to find one, partly because hardly any of the local taxi companies spoke English and communication was extremely difficult. Being left there without any practical assistance was incredibly stressful.

Unfortunately, things became even worse once we finally found a garage willing to repair the van.

Grúas Chiva would only communicate through our insurance company and were essentially unreachable when we tried to contact them directly. We called several times without getting through.

Through our insurer, specific times were arranged for the van to be delivered to a workshop. On both occasions, they were several hours late.

On one occasion, the vehicle was supposed to arrive at the garage around midday but did not arrive until late afternoon, although the workshop was only 15 minutes from the depot.

On the second occasion, delivery had been arranged for 9:30 am, but the van did not arrive until approximately 1:45 pm, despite the workshop being only around 10 minutes away. Because of this delay, the mechanic could no longer begin the repair that day and had to postpone the work until the following day.

When you are stranded abroad with a broken vehicle and completely dependent on a towing company to get the car to a workshop, reliability and communication are absolutely essential. Unfortunately, both were extremely poor in our experience.

We had no choice but to use this company because they had been arranged by our insurance. However, if you have the option of choosing your own towing service, or if your insurer suggests Grúas Chiva and offers alternatives, I would strongly recommend choosing another company.

The actual towing was not the issue. The lack of communication, repeated major delays and the way we were left to deal with the consequences ourselves made an already stressful experience even worse.

I cannot recommend them!

One of the most disappointing things about this City Hall is the feeling that not all citizens receive the same treatment.
From my experience at the Secretary's office, it seems that the criteria aren't always applied consistently: depending on who the person is, their circumstances, or their connections, the response can vary.
A City Hall should treat all its residents equally, with the same criteria, transparency, and objectivity. There shouldn't be the feeling that things are one way for some and another way for others.
We citizens deserve an impartial administration, where it doesn't matter who you are or who you know, but rather that the same criteria are applied to everyone.

one_star_reviews.text:
What a bunch of unprofessional people.
I requested an appointment to find out how to process my daughter's Youth Card and they told me they would contact me the next day at 9:00 a.m. The day arrived and, of course, there was no sign of life.
I've been a CaixaBank customer my whole life, as has my entire family. We have our salaries, our savings, and practically all our banking here. However, it seems that when a transaction doesn't generate any direct profit for the bank, customer service takes a back seat.

I'm convinced that if we had applied for a new card, insurance, or a loan, they probably would have attended to us immediately. But since it's simply a matter of processing the Youth Card, it seems it's not worth their time. The least I expect as a lifelong customer is to be treated with the same professionalism, regardless of whether the transaction generates any profit for the bank or not. Leaving a customer waiting and not even honoring the promise to call back at the agreed-upon time seems to me a lack of professionalism and respect.
Certainly, such service leaves much to be desired.
